title: preview.start joins the shared runtime command roster and every contract digest mirror is rotated
description:
SPIDR child 1 of task-dd86f35e117e4de1b5b885332d8af1f8, filed by architect-aa54e231 2026-09-06 under global rail 20 (spun-out rows) and epic rail 1 (a command kind is a four-row job).

WHY THIS ROW EXISTS - the architectural measurement that forced it. task-dd86f35e's DoD item 3 requires "a preview can be STARTED for a landed goal by a production path". Measured at HEAD on moe/work-2026-09-04:

(1) `moe-wrapper` (apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts) and `moe-daemon` (apps/daemon/src/daemon-main.ts) are SEPARATE bin entries in apps/daemon/package.json - separate OS processes sharing only the SQLite store.
(2) `createRepositoryDeliveryRuntime` (the node lander, the only place a landing reaches `outcome: "COMMITTED"`, node-lander.ts:255) is called from agent-wrapper-main.ts:160 and NOWHERE else. The landing hook lives in the WRAPPER process.
(3) `createPreviewSupervisor` holds live previews in an in-memory Map (preview-supervisor.ts:56 `const live = new Map(...)`). A preview started in the wrapper is invisible to the daemon: `supervisor.decide()` would find nothing and daemon shutdown could not sweep it.
(4) `preview.decide` arrives at the DAEMON's HTTP command plane. So the supervisor must live in the daemon.
(5) The daemon has NO tick/interval loop: `git grep -n "setInterval" -- apps/daemon/src` returns zero production hits. It is command- and read-driven only. A read must not spawn a product server.

Therefore the start trigger must be a DAEMON COMMAND, and because `runPreview` spawns a dev server and drives Playwright it must be an ASYNC command entry (the seam daemon-command-async-entries.ts already exists for exactly this - its own comment says the registry "is past its size cap, and this module is exactly the seam it spreads for async kinds").

A new runtime command kind is therefore unavoidable, and epic rail 1 binds: the shared-contract slice is its own row. This is that row. It publishes ONLY the kind on the shared contract; the daemon half is task-<CHILD-B>.

MEASURED MIRROR COUNT - THE DoD's "FOUR MIRRORS" IS A STALE FROZEN COUNT. `git grep -n 9057aa947ce5cd23c1e2e667ddbf9315a7e329869a4fa0d473e037cd1d30077d` over the tracked tree (excluding .moe/) returns SIX files, not four:
  packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts:935  (GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST, generated)
  packages/control-room-client/src/generated-coverage.test.ts:36      (CONTRACT_DIGEST; :35 also pins GENERATED_FILE_SHA256)
  apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts:18
  apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx:255
  apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan-reject.test.tsx:110
  apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/plan-run-resolution.test.tsx:149
task-bb0a7131's archive rationale already flagged approve-plan-reject.tsx as an unnamed FIFTH mirror; plan-run-resolution.test.tsx is a SIXTH that no prior row's list names. Do NOT trust this list either - epic rail 3 binds: re-run the grep for the LIVE digest immediately before editing and take the PRINTED result as authoritative.

CONTENTION: `commands.size` in packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-contract.test.ts was 104, then 110, then 115, then 118 inside a single row's flight (task-64d2757c's record). NEVER freeze that literal. Run the leg and take the PRINTED expected-vs-received.

PREDICT THE DIGEST BEFORE REGENERATING (task-64d2757c's reusable trick, worth 10 seconds): all mirrors verify AGREEMENT WITH the generator, never CORRECTNESS OF it. A ~6-line probe in packages/control-room-client importing deriveContractDigest() and RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS from the bare @moe/contracts specifier prints the digest independently. Regenerate with `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate` - NEVER hand-edit generated-client.ts.

THE KIND'S SHAPE (agreed with the consumer row so the two cannot disagree): `preview.start`, sorted slot between "policy.validate" and "preview.decide" in RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS (runtime-vocabulary.ts:104 area). Payload: exact keys ["goalId", "sha"]. It is an OPERATOR kind, human-only and MCP-excluded like preview.decide - but the FENCE and the payload decoder land in the consumer row, not here. This row publishes the kind and rotates the digest, nothing else.
definitionOfDone: "preview.start" is on RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS in packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts at its correct SORTED slot, verified by parsing the tuple itself (not the generated output, which sorts its own copy and would hide a source ordering defect). Assert the tuple has zero order defects and zero duplicates. Confirm the string was ABSENT immediately before the edit with `git grep -n "preview.start"` over apps/ and packages/.

packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-contract.test.ts carries the kind and its roster count is CORRECT AT HEAD. Do NOT freeze a count literal from this description: run the leg, take the PRINTED expected-vs-received as authoritative, and quote both numbers in the step note (epic rail 3).

The control-room client is REGENERATED via `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate`, never hand-edited, and generated-client.ts exposes a command builder for "preview.start" alongside the existing kinds.

EVERY digest mirror is rotated, censused by a full-tree `git grep -n <live-digest-hex>` across ALL file types (excluding .moe/ and node_modules) run BOTH before and after. Quote both censuses: zero hits of the OLD hex afterwards, and the after-count of the NEW hex stated as a number with the file list. The count is whatever the grep prints - six files at filing time, but a concurrent kind-publishing row moves it, so the printed result is authoritative, never this sentence.

GENERATED_FILE_SHA256 in packages/control-room-client/src/generated-coverage.test.ts is rotated with the digest, and packages/control-room-client/src/contract-digest.test.ts (which DERIVES the digest rather than agreeing with it) is green - so the value is correct by derivation, not merely self-consistent across mirrors.

At least two control-room digest mirrors are MUTATION-DRILLED separately and each goes RED with its own distinct refusal string; both drilled paths are `git status --porcelain`-checked before drilling and proven restored afterwards (global rail 13). Quote each red's message - one mirror passing does not prove another is watched.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines, each standalone and foreground: `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (MANDATORY - it is the only leg that loads the apps/control-room mirrors; the root `pnpm test` include has no apps/**), and `pnpm typecheck`. Repo-wide red is attributed by the merge-base-vs-HEAD path-attributed baseline (global rail 3) and disclosed verbatim.
taskRails: PUBLISH THE KIND ONLY. The daemon roster (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts, -families.ts, -payload-keys.ts), the MCP fence, the payload decoder and the async command entry all belong to the consumer row. Touching apps/daemon here is a scope breach that collides with its owner in the shared worktree.

NEVER FREEZE A ROSTER COUNT OR A DIGEST LITERAL (epic rail 3). commands.size moved three times inside one prior row's flight. Every count and every hex in this description is a LEAD to re-measure, never a value to assert against.
REGENERATE, NEVER HAND-EDIT. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate` owns generated-client.ts. A hand-edited generated file passes every mirror check while diverging from the generator.

`pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` is MANDATORY and NON-SUBSTITUTABLE. apps/control-room is in NONE of root `pnpm test` (vitest.config.ts include has no apps/**), `pnpm typecheck` (a digest is a string literal; tsc cannot see it), or the daemon leg. A forgotten mirror ships hard-throwing tests behind three green gates.

implementationPlan.description:
THE ROSTER ENTRY (DoD 1). Insert `"preview.start"` into `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` in packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts at its SORTED slot - immediately before `preview.decide`? No: verify by sorting, since `start` follows `decide` alphabetically. The neighbours at plan time are `"policy.install", "policy.validate", "preview.decide"` on :104.

VERIFY THE SLOT BY PARSING THE TUPLE ITSELF, not the generated output (DoD 1). The generator emits a sorted COPY (generate.ts:289), so a source-order mistake is invisible downstream - the generated client would look correct while the tuple was wrong. The arm that actually catches it is runtime-contract.test.ts:117-125, which asserts the tuple equals its own sort against the PRODUCTION tuple; its comment records the incident that earned it, where a kind landed at a wrong position, was copied into the hand transcription at the same wrong position, and both stayed green.

That single insertion is the whole production edit. Do NOT add a payload type: generate.ts:37-39 states "Payloads stay JsonObject. No per-kind payload schema exists in the contract, and generating per-kind payload types would invent a contract that does not exist." The payload KEYS belong to the daemon half, task-dbc79d2556ab4.

THE HAND TRANSCRIPTION AND THE COUNT (DoD 2), in packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-contract.test.ts.

1. Insert `"preview.start"` into `EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS` (:35) at the SAME sorted position as step 2.
2. Move the `expect(commands.size).toBe(N)` literal (:109 at plan time, reading 118) by exactly ONE.

TAKE THE NUMBER FROM THE PRINTED EXPECTED-VS-RECEIVED, not from this plan. DoD 2 says so explicitly and the history proves it: that literal read 104 yesterday morning, 110 last night and 118 at plan time. Run the leg, let it fail, use what it prints.

DO NOT DERIVE THE EXPECTED LIST FROM THE TUPLE. The file's header at :29-34 explains that an expectation computed from the tuple under test can never fail - that is the vacuous arm this transcription replaced. Hand-copy the entry; the deliberate edit IS the test.

Check the other transcribed rosters in the same file before moving on - `RUNTIME_QUERY_KINDS` and `RUNTIME_TELEMETRY_KINDS` are pinned by hand too. This row adds a COMMAND kind, so neither should move; confirm rather than assume.

REGENERATE THE CLIENT (DoD 3). `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate` - never a hand edit.

Capture for the completion record: the exact command, the OLD digest read from generated-client.ts BEFORE regenerating, and the NEW digest after.

AN UNCHANGED DIGEST IS A STOP, NOT A PASS (DoD 3). It means the generator did not see the new kind - the roster edit never reached `canonicalContractSurface()` (contract-digest.ts, hashed by `deriveContractDigest()`). Investigate rather than proceeding.

CONFIRM generated-client.ts EXPOSES A COMMAND BUILDER for `preview.start` alongside the existing kinds, not merely that the string appears. The row asks for the builder because that is what a consumer actually calls.

Then `git diff --stat packages/control-room-client/src/generated/` and confirm the only changes are the new kind and the digest. Unrelated churn means the committed artifact was stale before you started - disclose it verbatim rather than absorbing it.

NOTE WHAT MUST **NOT** BE EDITED: packages/control-room-client/src/contract-digest.test.ts DERIVES the digest and compares, so it goes green on its own. If it needs an edit, the regeneration did not do what it should have - stop and find out why. Editing it would turn a real check into a tautology.

ROTATE ALL FIVE TRANSCRIBED MIRRORS PLUS THE FILE HASH (DoD 4 and 5). None of these follows a regeneration; each is a hand edit, and they are why this row is eight files rather than three.

Using the census from step 1 - NOT the list here - update every hit of the OLD hex to the NEW one:
  packages/control-room-client/src/generated-coverage.test.ts:36  `const CONTRACT_DIGEST`
  apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts:18
  apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx:255
  apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan-reject.test.tsx:110
  apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/plan-run-resolution.test.tsx:149

AND ROTATE `GENERATED_FILE_SHA256` at generated-coverage.test.ts:35 (DoD 5). It is a DIFFERENT value - a sha256 over the generated file's bytes, asserted at :164 as `createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex")`. Regenerating the client changes those bytes. A census for the digest hex will never find it, so it is the likeliest omission in the whole row. Compute it from the regenerated file rather than copying a number.

THEN RE-CENSUS AND ASSERT ZERO STALE (DoD 4, second half): `git grep -n "<OLD hex>" -- . ':!.moe' ':!pnpm-lock.yaml' ':!.serena'` must return NOTHING, and a census for the NEW hex must return the same file set as before with the new value. Quote both censuses - that command, not a visual check, is the evidence.

THE MUTATION DRILL ON TWO CONTROL-ROOM MIRRORS (DoD 6) - the row's most valuable artifact, because it is the only proof the apps/control-room mirrors are covered by any gate at all.

DRILL TWO SEPARATELY, each going RED with its OWN DISTINCT refusal string. Pick two from different files - for example data-adapter.test.ts and one of the three `.tsx` mirrors - so the drill shows the coverage is not a single shared assertion.

For each: `git status --porcelain <path>` BEFORE drilling (global rail on drill restore proof), revert ONLY that mirror to the OLD hex, run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, quote the FAILING LINE and the refusal string, then restore and prove the restore. All five mirrors are TRACKED, so `git diff -- <path>` returning empty is a valid restore proof here.

RECORD BOTH REFUSAL STRINGS. If two mirrors produce the SAME message, say so - it means one gate covers both and the second drill proved less than it appears to. If a mirror can be reverted and the suite stays GREEN, that mirror is unguarded: report it rather than quietly fixing it, because an unguarded mirror is a finding about the gate, not about this row.

`pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` is the only leg that sees these files - the root lane has no `apps/**` in its include, and neither typecheck nor the daemon leg reaches them.

GATES AND SELF-REVIEW (DoD 7). Each leg standalone and FOREGROUND, each quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line; an exit-0 leg with no count line RAN NOTHING, and `pnpm --filter <pkg>` exits 0 with "No projects matched the filters" for a name that is not a workspace package:
- `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test`
- `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test`
- `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` - MANDATORY: it is the ONLY leg that sees the four apps/control-room mirrors.
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm test` (root) - state plainly that the root lane covers NO `apps/**` file, so it is not evidence for four of the six mirrors.

SELF-REVIEW:
- Did contract-digest.test.ts go green WITHOUT being edited? If you edited it, revert and find out why the regeneration failed.
- Is the tuple SORTED at source? Move the entry to a wrong slot and confirm runtime-contract.test.ts:117-125 reds; restore. The generator's sorted copy would have hidden it.
- Did the count come from the printed expected-vs-received rather than from this plan?
- Did the census find exactly the mirrors you edited - no seventh, none missed? Re-run it.
- Did `GENERATED_FILE_SHA256` rotate? It is the one value the digest census cannot see.
- ZERO daemon-side edits: `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/` must be EMPTY. The payload keys, the registry entry and the fence are task-dbc79d2556ab4's.

PATH-ATTRIBUTED BASELINE: merge-base failures, HEAD failures, subtract, intersect with this row's owned paths; complete only when that intersection is EMPTY. Expect foreign timeout reds from host handle exhaustion and disclose them verbatim with paths rather than re-running the suite repeatedly, which degrades every other seat's gate.
